# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 20 LOST MARGARET

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

It proved possible for Nell to continue her existence; eventually, a day arrived in which one of Miss Winifred’s remarks caused her to smile once more. Yet contained within that smile was a quality that had previously never existed in Nell’s smile, one that would henceforth remain a permanent part of it.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0000 }

Hugh brought her down to Seven Gulls Point on the initial day she could manage a drive, leaving her at that location while he made the row across the channel to visit a patient located at the fishing village. Across the dunes and the harbor, a buoyant wind was racing, churning the water up into white-caps and sweeping over the sandshore using lengthy rows of silvery breakers.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0001 }

“It makes me truly proud to have you back here, Mistress Carrow,” Captain Saul stated. “Have a seat—have a seat. I’m afraid this place is dreadfully dusty today—yet one doesn't need to gaze at dust when such scenery is right there to be seen, does one?”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0002 }

“The dust doesn’t bother me,” Nell stated, “however, Hugh insists that I remain outdoors. I believe I will head down to those rocks and sit.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0003 }

“Do you want someone with you, or do you prefer to be by yourself?”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0004 }

“Should you be referring to your own presence when you speak of company, I would far prefer it to being by myself,” Nell said, offering a smile. A sigh followed her words. Being by herself had never bothered her in the past. At present, it filled her with dread. These days, whenever she found herself on her own, a terrible sense of isolation consumed her.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0005 }

“In this pleasant small location, you are protected from the wind,” Captain Saul remarked upon their arrival at the rocks. “This is a place where I frequently sit. Simply sitting and dreaming here is wonderful.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0006 }

“Oh—dreams,” Nell let out a sigh. “Captain Saul, I am unable to dream now—dreams are behind me.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0007 }

“Oh, no, you’re not, Mistress Carrow—oh, no, you’re not,” Captain Saul remarked thoughtfully. “I understand your current feelings—however, provided you remain alive, joy will return to you, and before you realize it, dreaming will resume—we must express gratitude to the Lord for that! Without the dreams we have, interring us might as well happen. In what way could we endure existence were it not for our immortality dream? Furthermore, Mistress Carrow, that specific dream is CERTAIN to be realized. Some day, your little Joyce will be seen by you again.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0008 }

“However, my baby will no longer be mine,” Nell uttered, her lips quivering. “Oh, it is possible she will turn out to be, in the words of Longfellow, 'a fair maiden clothed with celestial grace’—yet she is going to be an unfamiliar person to me.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0009 }

“I think God is going to handle things better than THAT,” Captain Saul remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0010 }

The pair remained quiet for a brief moment. After that, Captain Saul spoke in a very soft voice:
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0011 }

“Mistress Carrow, can I speak to you regarding lost Margaret?”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0012 }

“Naturally,” Nell softly replied. Though she lacked knowledge of who “lost Margaret” might be, she sensed she was about to be told the story of Captain Saul’s romantic past.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0013 }

“I’ve frequently wished to speak to you regarding her,” Captain Saul continued.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0014 }

“Do you know why, Mistress Carrow? It’s because I desire someone to recall and hold her in their thoughts occasionally once I have passed away. I cannot endure the thought that every living person will forget her name. And currently, I am the sole person who still remembers lost Margaret.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0015 }

Captain Saul subsequently recounted the tale—a ancient, long-lost narrative, because more than fifty years had elapsed since Margaret had dozed off one afternoon inside her father’s dory and floated—or at least that was the assumption, since her ultimate destiny was never definitely determined—away from the channel, past the bar, to meet her end in the dark thundersquall that had arisen so abruptly on that distant summer afternoon. Yet for Captain Saul, those fifty years seemed like nothing more than yesterday when it has gone.
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0016 }

“Following that event, I spent months pacing the coastline,” he uttered sorrowfully, “hoping to locate her beloved, darling small corpse; yet the ocean failed to return her to me. However, I will locate her eventually, Mistress Carrow—I will locate her eventually. She waits for me. I would like to describe to you precisely how she appeared, yet I am unable to do so. Over the sandbar at dawn, I have observed a delicate, silver fog that resembled her—and on other occasions, I have noticed a white birch tree in those woods back there that reminded me of her. She possessed light, brown locks and a small, fair, lovely visage, alongside long, thin fingers similar to yours, Mistress Carrow, though darker, because she was raised on the coast. At times, I awaken during the night to the ocean summoning me as it used to, and it feels as though missing Margaret were shouting within it. Furthermore, during a tempest when the swells weep and groan, I detect her weeping in their midst. And whenever they giggle on a bright afternoon, it is HER giggle—missing Margaret’s lovely, playful, small giggle. I lost her to the ocean, yet eventually I will locate her. Mistress Carrow. It is impossible for it to separate us eternally.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0017 }

“It pleases me that you shared information regarding her with me,” Nell remarked. “I frequently pondered the reason you resided by yourself for your entire existence.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0018 }

“I could never love another person. Lost Margaret carried my heart away with her—out there,” declared the elderly lover, who had remained devoted for half a century to the sweetheart he lost to the sea. “You will not care if I speak of her frequently, will you, Mistress Carrow? I find joy in it—since the sorrow vanished from her recollection many years back and simply gave its benediction instead. I am certain you will always remember her, Mistress Carrow. And should the coming years, as I trust they will, grant more young ones to your household, I desire your word that you will recount to THEM the tale of lost Margaret, ensuring her memory does not perish among humanity.”
{: #nw-v04-c20-p0019 }
